docs.title: Welcome
docs.text:
Simple-Wiki is a personal markdown wiki — wiki links, search, uploads, revision history, templates, and an admin dashboard. Most people run it on a home network or NAS.

The home page with sidebar table of contents and a built-in syntax cheat sheet.

This guide covers using the wiki. For installation, Docker, and server settings, see the project README.

docs.title: What you can do
docs.text:
Role Capabilities Visitor Read, search, tweak reading settings (when public read is on) Editor Create and edit pages, upload files, view history, restore revisions, use extensions Admin All of the above, plus users, backups, extensions, and revision limits

Every account can edit

There are no read-only editors. Only create accounts for people you trust.

docs.title: Where to start
docs.text:
• New to the wiki? First login then Navigation
  • Want to write? Editing basics
  • Running the wiki? Admin dashboard

docs.title: Built-in help
docs.text: Your wiki also has a help article at /wiki/help. Open it from the gear icon → Help, or visit that URL directly.

docs.title: Accounts & access
docs.text: Visitors can browse without signing in when public read is enabled. Editors sign in via this form.

docs.title: Public read vs private wiki
docs.text:
On most home-network setups, public read is on — anyone can browse and search without an account. That's the default.

If your wiki is on the public internet, the person who hosts it may turn public read off (PUBLIC_READ=false). Then every page requires a login.

docs.title: Roles
docs.text:
Role What you can do Visitor Read and search (when public read is on), change reading settings Editor Everything above, plus create and edit pages, upload files, restore revisions, use extensions Admin Everything above, plus the admin dashboard: users, backups, extension toggles, revision limits

Every account can edit everything

There is no read-only editor role. If someone has an account, they can edit any page. Only give accounts to people you trust with the whole wiki.

docs.title: Signing in
docs.text:
1. Click Sign in in the header (or go to /login)
  2. Enter your username and password
  3. Use the eye icon to show or hide your password while typing

After a successful login, you return to the page you were on. If you clicked something that required login first, the URL may include ?next=/some/path to send you back there.

docs.title: Password rules
docs.text:
• At least 8 characters
  • Every new account must change its password on first login
  • After that, any signed-in user can change their password at /admin/change-password
  • Admins also have a Password link in the admin dashboard header

On first login, set your new password before doing anything else on the wiki.

docs.title: Signing out
docs.text: Click Sign out in the header.

docs.title: Who needs an account?
docs.text: Task Account required? Read pages (public wiki) No Search No Create or edit pages Yes Upload files Yes View history / restore revisions Yes Admin dashboard Yes (admin role)

docs.title: Too many login attempts
docs.text: After several failed sign-in attempts, you'll be asked to wait before trying again (about 15 minutes). This is normal — wait it out, or double-check your username and password.

docs.title: Family trees
docs.text:
The family tree list at /family-tree.

The Family Tree extension adds interactive genealogy trees you can embed in any article.

Anyone can view trees. Creating, editing, and deleting trees requires a signed-in account.

docs.title: Finding trees
docs.text:
Go to /family-tree, or Admin → Extensions → Open next to Family Tree.

Action Who Browse and open trees Everyone New tree / Delete Signed-in users

docs.title: Tree editor
docs.text: At /family-tree/[slug] you'll see a sidebar and a canvas.

docs.title: Sidebar — person details
docs.text:
Select a person to edit:

  • Name — supports [[wiki links]] to biography pages
  • Birth year / Death year
  • Photo — upload an image

Drag the divider between sidebar and canvas to resize. Your preferred width is saved in the browser.

docs.title: Canvas — relationships
docs.text:
• Add child, Add spouse, Add parent
  • Link existing parent — connect to someone already in the tree
  • Remove person
  • Pan — drag the canvas
  • Zoom — scroll wheel
  • Recenter — top-right button
  • Click a person to highlight their paternal line

Click Save when you're done. The editor warns you if you try to leave with unsaved changes. If someone else saved first, use Reload latest or Overwrite with mine.

On phones, the person sidebar stacks under the canvas.

docs.title: Embedding in articles
docs.text:
{{FamilyTree|family=smith-family}}

The slug matches the tree URL (/family-tree/smith-family).

From the page editor, use the Family Tree toolbar menu to insert an existing tree or create a new one inline.

In the rendered article:

  • Readers can pan and zoom the embedded tree
  • Signed-in editors see an Edit tree link on the embed

docs.title: Disabling the extension
docs.text: Admin → Extensions → toggle Family Tree off. Routes return 404, embeds stop rendering, and the toolbar button disappears.

docs.title: Tips
docs.text:
• Link person names to wiki articles with [[wiki links]]
  • Photos go to the same /uploads/ folder as other wiki files

docs.title: Revision history
docs.text:
Per-page history with edit summaries and expandable diffs.

Every time you save a page, Simple-Wiki stores a new revision. You can look back at older versions, see what changed, and restore an earlier state if you need to.

docs.title: Per-page history
docs.text:
On any article, click History next to Edit (you must be signed in to see those buttons).

The history page lists revisions newest-first. Each entry shows:

  • When the edit happened
  • The edit summary, if the editor wrote one
  • An expandable diff against the next newer version (title changes included)

Restore is only available when you're signed in. Click Restore this version, confirm, and the wiki creates a new revision from that snapshot. Nothing in between is erased — you're just adding another version on top.

docs.title: Recent changes
docs.text:
The /recent feed groups edits by day with expandable diffs.

The Recent changes page shows the last 100 edits across the whole wiki, grouped by day. Expand any entry to load its diff.

Open it at /recent, or go to Admin → Recent Changes.

docs.title: Revision retention
docs.text:
By default, every revision is kept forever. Admins can cap how many revisions are stored per page:

  1. Go to Admin → Recent Changes (or /recent → Settings)
  2. Set Max revisions per page — leave blank for unlimited
  3. Save

When a limit is set, the oldest revisions are removed automatically. The live page content is not affected.

docs.title: Edit summaries
docs.text: The Edit summary field in the editor is optional, but worth using on bigger edits. Summaries show up in both per-page history and recent changes, which makes it much easier to scan what happened.

docs.title: Tips
docs.text:
• Restoring never deletes history — it adds a new revision
  • If you get a conflict while editing, use Reload latest or Overwrite with mine. History still shows what changed.

docs.title: Cannot sign in
docs.text: Problem What to try Forgot admin password In Docker: docker exec <container> node scripts/reset-password.mjs admin (prints a new temp password). Locally: bun run reset-password -- admin. Or check first-boot server logs "Invalid username or password" Check caps lock. Usernames are case-sensitive Redirected to change password Normal on first login — set a new password at /admin/change-password "Too many login attempts" Wait about 15 minutes, then try again Page requires login to read Public read may be off — sign in, or ask your host to enable PUBLIC_READ

docs.title: Page won't save
docs.text: Problem What to try Edit conflict Use Reload latest or Overwrite with mine on the banner Content too large Page markdown is limited to 2 MB per save (uploads don't count) Not signed in Sign in first "Too many requests" You hit a rate limit — wait a minute and retry Duplicate page A page at that address already exists — open it and edit instead

docs.title: Broken images or links
docs.text: Problem What to try Broken image Check Admin → Files — the upload may have been deleted Red wiki link The target page doesn't exist yet — click to create it (signed in) Can't delete a file A page still references it — remove the reference first

docs.title: Search returns nothing
docs.text:
• Type at least three characters for header suggestions
  • Search covers articles and help pages — try simpler, plain-text words

docs.title: History and diffs
docs.text: Problem What to try "Diff too large to display" The change is saved; the diff is just too big to show inline. You can still restore Can't restore You must be signed in. Refresh the history page if the restore button fails

docs.title: Family tree issues
docs.text: Problem What to try Embed is empty Check Admin → Extensions — Family Tree must be enabled. Verify the family= slug matches a real tree Changes not saved Click Save in the tree editor. Don't leave with unsaved changes Edit conflict Use Reload latest or Overwrite with mine — same choices as wiki page conflicts

docs.title: Backup import
docs.text: Problem What to try Import fails Use a valid Simple-Wiki backup zip. Check Fully overwrite existing database 413 / too large Increase BODY_SIZE_LIMIT (defaults to 512M with bun run start / Docker) and restart 503 during import Normal — the database is swapping. Wait a few seconds and refresh Missing uploads Enable Restore uploads during import. Files on disk that aren't in the backup are kept

docs.title: Browser issues
docs.text: Problem What to try Blank or stuck page Hard refresh (++Cmd+Shift+R++ on Mac, ++Ctrl+Shift+R++ on Windows). Try disabling browser extensions on localhost Reading settings lost They're stored per browser — they don't sync Theme resets Make sure cookies are enabled

docs.title: Still stuck?
docs.text:
• Read the built-in help at /wiki/help on your wiki
  • See the project README for installation and hosting
  • Open an issue on GitHub

docs.title: Admin dashboard
docs.text:
The admin dashboard with page search, listing, and actions.

The admin dashboard at /admin is for users with the admin role. Click Admin in the header after signing in.

docs.title: Tabs
docs.text: Tab What you do there Pages Search, view, edit, delete, and create pages Files Browse, preview, rename, and delete uploads Recent Changes Site-wide edit feed + revision retention settings Templates Manage template-namespace pages Extensions Enable or disable bundled extensions Users Create, promote/demote, and delete accounts Backups Export and import the wiki

docs.title: Pages
docs.text:
Search and paginate through all pages (100 per page).

Action Notes View / Edit Open the page Delete Removes the page New page Opens the editor

docs.title: Files
docs.text: See Uploads for rename and delete behavior.

docs.title: Recent Changes
docs.text: Same feed as /recent, plus revision retention controls inline.

docs.title: Templates
docs.text: Lists template-namespace pages. New page opens the editor with namespace set to template.

docs.title: Change password
docs.text: The Password link in the admin header goes to /admin/change-password. Any signed-in user can use that URL, not just admins.

docs.title: Wiki name
docs.text: The name shown in the admin UI and backups comes from the WIKI_NAME environment variable, set by whoever hosts the wiki.

docs.title: Backups
docs.text:
Export and import wiki backups as zip files.

Admin → Backups lets you download a snapshot of the wiki or restore from one.

docs.title: Export
docs.text:
Click Export backup for a zip containing:

  • wiki.db — always included
  • manifest.txt — wiki name and export date
  • Uploaded files — optional (the UI warns when that library is large; export loads uploads into memory)
  • markdown/ folder — raw page exports with YAML frontmatter — optional

Keep backups somewhere safe, not just on the same machine as the wiki.

docs.title: Import
docs.text:
Import replaces your live data. Read the checkboxes carefully.

  1. Upload a backup zip
  2. Check Fully overwrite existing database (required)
  3. Optionally check Restore uploads to merge files from the backup
  4. Click Import

While the database swaps, other users see a 503 page. It usually takes a few seconds.

If something goes wrong, the import rolls back automatically.

docs.title: Upload merge
docs.text: Situation What happens File in backup, already on disk Overwritten File in backup, not on disk Added File on disk, not in backup Kept — not deleted

docs.title: When to back up
docs.text:
• Before importing a backup
  • Before bulk edits or upgrades
  • Regularly, if people edit the wiki often

docs.title: Tips
docs.text:
• Include uploads if your wiki has lots of images
  • The markdown export is handy for reading content outside the wiki
  • Test a restore on a copy before relying on a backup in production

docs.title: Extensions
docs.text:
Enable or disable bundled extensions.

Extensions add features beyond the core wiki. They're built into the app — you enable or disable them here, not install new ones from the UI.

docs.title: Admin → Extensions
docs.text:
Column Meaning Name / Version / Description What the extension is Enabled On/off toggle — takes effect immediately Manage Link to the extension's page (if it has one)

When an extension is off:

  • Its pages return 404
  • Embeds like {{FamilyTree}} don't render
  • Toolbar buttons and sidebar links disappear

docs.title: Family Tree
docs.text:
The main extension in production builds:

  • /family-tree — manage trees
  • {{FamilyTree|family=slug}} — embed in articles
  • Toolbar integration in the page editor

See Family trees.

docs.title: Adding new extensions
docs.text:
New extensions are added by a developer editing the source code — see the project README.

Trust matters

Extensions run code at server startup. Only use extensions you wrote or fully trust.

docs.title: User management
docs.text:
Create accounts and manage roles from Admin → Users.

Admins manage accounts under Admin → Users.

docs.title: Creating a user
docs.text:
1. Go to Admin → Users
  2. Enter a username (letters, numbers, underscores, hyphens)
  3. Check Admin if they need dashboard access
  4. Click Create user

A one-time password appears on screen. Copy it with the button — it won't be shown again. Send it to the new user securely.

They must change that password on first login.

docs.title: User list
docs.text: Column Meaning Username Login name Role Admin or Editor Must change password Waiting on first-login password change Created When the account was made Actions Promote / demote, or delete

docs.title: Roles
docs.text:
• Editor — can edit pages, upload files, use extensions
  • Admin — all of the above, plus the admin dashboard

Use Promote / Demote in the actions column to change a role. You can’t demote or delete the last admin, and you can’t delete your own account.

docs.title: Deleting a user
docs.text: Click the delete button next to the user and confirm. Their sessions end immediately.

docs.title: If someone loses their password
docs.text:
Ask whoever hosts the wiki to reset it from the shell:

docker exec <container> node scripts/reset-password.mjs <username>

That prints a new temporary password. List accounts with --list. Locally: bun run reset-password -- <username>.

docs.title: Tips
docs.text:
• Only make someone an admin if they need to manage users, backups, or extensions
  • Usernames can't be changed after creation

docs.title: Editing basics
docs.text: The editor with markdown source, live preview, toolbar, and infobox panel.

docs.title: Ways to create a page
docs.text: How Where New page button Header (signed in) Red wiki link Click a [[Page Title]] link to a page that doesn't exist yet Search Create "[query]" when search finds nothing (signed in) Admin Admin → Pages → New page

docs.title: The editor
docs.text:
You'll see a split view:

  • Left — markdown source
  • Right — live preview (updates as you type, no server round-trip)

Toggle preview with the button in the toolbar. On desktop, preview starts open. Your preference is remembered in the browser.

docs.title: Fields
docs.text:
Field Purpose Title The name shown at the top of the page Namespace article (normal), template, or help Edit summary Short note about what you changed (optional, shows in history) Content The markdown body

New pages get an address like /wiki/my-page based on the title you enter.

docs.title: Toolbar
docs.text: Quick inserts for formatting, wiki links, references, callouts, infoboxes, image boxes, uploads, and family trees (when the extension is enabled).

docs.title: Tab key
docs.text: Press ++Tab++ in the markdown pane to indent. ++Shift+Tab++ outdents.

docs.title: Saving and canceling
docs.text:
Save publishes your changes and adds a revision to history.

Cancel returns to the article without saving.

If you've typed anything, the editor warns you before navigating away or closing the tab.

docs.title: Edit conflicts
docs.text:
If someone else saved while you were editing, the editor shows a conflict banner with two choices:

  • Reload latest — discard your draft and load their version
  • Overwrite with mine — keep your draft and replace what’s on the server

docs.title: Editing an existing page
docs.text: Open the article and click Edit (signed in). The editor loads the current title and content.

docs.title: Namespaces
docs.text:
Namespace Use article Normal wiki pages — searchable, listed on /pages template Reusable {{TemplateName}} blocks help Help content (the built-in /wiki/help page uses this)

Most pages should be article.

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
• Markdown & wiki links
  • Templates
  • Uploads
  • References

docs.title: Markdown & wiki links
docs.text: Simple-Wiki uses standard markdown plus GitHub Flavored Markdown (tables, strikethrough, task lists).

docs.title: Basics
docs.text:
# Heading 1

## Heading 2

**bold** and _italic_

- Bullet
- List

1. Numbered
2. List

[External link](https://example.com)

`inline code`

docs.title: Code blocks
docs.text:
```python
def hello():
    print("Hello")
```

Add a language name after the opening backticks for syntax highlighting.

docs.title: Tables
docs.text:
| Column | Value |
| ------ | ----- |
| Name   | Ada   |

docs.title: Task lists
docs.text:
- [x] Done
- [ ] Todo

docs.title: Wiki links
docs.text:
Link to other pages on your wiki:

[[Page Title]]
[[Page Title|custom label]]
  • Existing pages → blue link
  • Missing pages → red link (click to create, if signed in)
  • Works in infoboxes, family tree names, and reference sources

docs.title: Headings and sidebar TOC
docs.text: # through #### become headings. Levels 1–4 show up in the article sidebar on long pages.

docs.title: Quick reference
docs.text:
Syntax Result [[Page Title]] Wiki link [[Title\|label]] Wiki link with custom text **bold** bold *italic* italic `code` code ~~strike~~ ~~strike~~

For infoboxes, callouts, and galleries, see Templates.

docs.title: References
docs.text: Add footnote-style citations that appear as a References section at the bottom of the page.

docs.title: Inline (easiest)
docs.text:
Put the source right in the marker. Numbers are assigned in order of appearance:

Einstein published special relativity in 1905.[^: [On the Electrodynamics of Moving Bodies](https://example.com)]

Click Reference in the editor toolbar to insert this.

docs.title: Paired markers
docs.text:
Put [^] in the text and matching [^]: lines at the bottom:

First claim.[^] Second claim.[^]

[^]: First source
[^]: Second source

They're matched in order — you don't number them yourself.

docs.title: What sources can contain
docs.text:
• Plain text: [^: Published in Nature, 2020]
  • A link: [^: [Article title](https://example.com)]
  • A wiki link: [^: [[Related Page]]]

docs.title: On the rendered page
docs.text:
Citation numbers in the text jump to the References section. Clicking one briefly highlights the matching entry.

The References heading only appears when the page actually has citations.

docs.title: Tips
docs.text:
• One-off citations → inline [^: ...]
  • Many sources → paired [^] / [^]: at the bottom
  • Both styles can mix on the same page

docs.title: Templates
docs.text: Templates are reusable blocks you drop into articles — infoboxes, image galleries, callouts, and your own custom layouts.

docs.title: Infobox
docs.text:
A summary box that floats to the right of the article text:

{{Infobox|title=Ada Lovelace|Born=1815|Died=1852|Known for=Computing}}

Click Infobox in the editor toolbar to open the visual editor. Pick Basic, Person, or Country for preset fields. You can upload an image and drag rows to reorder them.

docs.title: Image box
docs.text:
A gallery with captions:

{{ImageBox|@img0=photo.jpg|@img0_cap=Front view|columns=2}}

Use the ImageBox toolbar button. Upload images per slot, set captions and column count, and drag to reorder images.

docs.title: Callouts
docs.text:
{{Note|Helpful context for the reader.}}
{{Warning|Something to watch out for.}}

docs.title: Stub banner
docs.text:
{{Stub}}

Marks the article as incomplete.

docs.title: Custom templates
docs.text:
Make a page in the template namespace, then call it from any article:

{{Character|name=Alice|role=Editor}}

Template body example (namespace: template, title: Character):

**Name:** {{{name}}}
**Role:** {{{role}}}

Placeholders use {{{param_name}}}.

Manage them under Admin → Templates or at /pages?ns=template.

docs.title: Family tree embed
docs.text:
{{FamilyTree|family=my-family-slug}}

See Family trees.

docs.title: Toolbar shortcuts
docs.text: The editor toolbar inserts the right syntax for Note, Warning, Infobox, ImageBox, and Family Tree at your cursor.

docs.title: Uploads
docs.text: Signed-in users can upload images and files.

docs.title: From the editor
docs.text:
Upload button — pick a file; the markdown link is inserted at your cursor:

  • Images → ![filename](url)
  • Other files → [filename](url)

Drag and drop — drop a file onto the markdown pane. Same result.

Infobox / ImageBox panels — each has its own upload button per image slot.

Family tree person photos work the same way in the tree editor. See Family trees.

docs.title: Using uploads in markdown
docs.text:
Files are served at /uploads/[filename]:

![Diagram](/uploads/diagram.png)
[Download PDF](/uploads/report.pdf)

docs.title: Admin → Files
docs.text: Admins can browse, preview, rename, and delete uploads. Renaming a file updates its links across the wiki automatically.

docs.title: Tips
docs.text: • Descriptive filenames help — they show up in your markdown

docs.title: First login
docs.text:
The sign-in form at /login.

The first time Simple-Wiki starts with an empty database, it creates an admin account. This only happens once.

docs.title: Getting the password
docs.text:
Default: the server prints a random one-time password in the terminal:

[auth] Created initial admin user.
[auth]   Username: admin
[auth]   One-time password: <random-password>

Ask whoever installed the wiki, or check the logs from that first startup. The password is shown exactly once.

Alternative: the installer can set ADMIN_PASSWORD in .env before the first start (at least 8 characters). Use that value to sign in.

Only applies on first boot

Setting ADMIN_PASSWORD later does nothing. It only works when the admin account is first created. To start over, delete wiki.db and restart — but you'll lose all wiki data.

docs.title: Signing in for the first time
docs.text:
1. Go to /login or click Sign in
  2. Username: admin
  3. Enter the initial password
  4. You'll be sent to Change password — pick something new (8+ characters)

Every new account, not just admin, must change its password on first login.

docs.title: Adding more users
docs.text:
As admin, go to Admin → Users to create editor accounts. Each gets a one-time password shown once at creation.

See User management.

docs.title: Navigation
docs.text: The header search bar, sign-in link, and reading settings. Article pages show a sidebar with a table of contents.

docs.title: Header
docs.text:
The header stays at the top on every page.

Element What it does Logo Home page Search Live suggestions after three characters; press ++Enter++ for full results New page Create a page (signed-in users only) Admin Admin dashboard (admins only) Sign in / Sign out Log in or out Gear icon Reading settings — font, size, column width, Help, About Theme toggle Light or dark mode

docs.title: Sidebar (on articles only)
docs.text:
On the home page and wiki articles (/ and /wiki/...), you may see a left sidebar with:

  • Table of contents — headings from the current article
  • Extension links — optional, if an enabled extension adds them

Collapse it with the arrow on desktop. On mobile, use the hamburger menu.

docs.title: Pages worth bookmarking
docs.text: Page URL All articles /pages All templates /pages?ns=template Recent changes /recent Built-in help /wiki/help Family trees /family-tree

docs.title: About
docs.text: Gear icon → About shows the wiki version, build date, and source commit.

docs.title: Skip link
docs.text: Press ++Tab++ on page load to jump to the Skip to content link.

docs.title: Reading pages
docs.text: A typical article page with title, last-edited time, and rendered markdown content.

docs.title: Home page
docs.text:
The home page (/) shows the article stored as home. On a fresh install, that's a welcome page with tips and a syntax cheat sheet.

If home doesn't exist yet, you'll see a short placeholder instead.

docs.title: Articles
docs.text:
Wiki pages live at /wiki/[slug] — for example, /wiki/my-page.

Each article shows:

  • The page title
  • When it was last edited
  • Edit and History buttons (signed-in users only)
  • Rendered markdown — syntax highlighting, tables, callouts, infoboxes, embedded family trees, and so on

docs.title: Table of contents
docs.text: Long articles get a table of contents in the sidebar (headings level 1–4). Click a heading to jump to that section.

docs.title: Wiki links
docs.text:
[[Page Title]] links to another page. Existing pages show as normal blue links.

Red links mean the page doesn't exist yet. If you're signed in, clicking one lets you create it.

docs.title: Images
docs.text: Click an image to open a lightbox. Use arrow keys or the on-screen controls to zoom and move between images.

docs.title: References
docs.text:
Pages with citations get a References section at the bottom. Click a citation number to jump to the source.

See References for how to write them.

docs.title: Browsing all pages
docs.text: Go to /pages for an alphabetical list of articles, or /pages?ns=template for templates.

docs.title: Reading preferences
docs.text:
Font, text size, column width, and links to Help and About.

Click the gear icon in the header to adjust how articles look. Everything here is saved in your browser and applies across the whole wiki.

docs.title: Font
docs.text: Six options: Atkinson Hyperlegible (default), Georgia, Roboto, Merriweather, Space Mono, and Lato.

docs.title: Text size
docs.text: Small, Medium, or Large.

docs.title: Column width
docs.text: On desktop, drag the slider to narrow or widen the text column. Handy on wide monitors where long lines are hard to read.

docs.title: Theme
docs.text: The sun/moon toggle next to the gear switches light and dark mode. Saved in a cookie.

docs.title: Help and About
docs.text:
• Help — opens /wiki/help
  • About — wiki version and build info

Per browser

These settings don't sync between devices or browsers. Set them up on each machine you read from.

docs.title: Search
docs.text: Full-text search results with highlighted snippets.

docs.title: Header search
docs.text:
The search box in the header is the fastest way to find something:

  1. Type at least three characters
  2. Up to eight suggestions appear
  3. Use ++Up++ / ++Down++ to move, ++Enter++ to open, ++Escape++ to close
  4. View all results opens the full search page

docs.title: Full results
docs.text:
Press ++Enter++ in the header search, or go to /search?q=your+query.

You'll see matching pages with highlighted snippets. If you're signed in and nothing matches, you can Create "[query]" to start a new page with that title.

docs.title: What's searchable
docs.text: Search covers articles and help pages, like the built-in /wiki/help. Just type the words you'd expect to find on the page.
